newsitem.title: CHINA: China tells media HK handover news should be good.
newsitem.headline: China tells media HK handover news should be good.

text.p: China has told its state-run broadcasters to emphasise good news to create a positive atmosphere in the run-up to the return of Hong Kong to Beijing rule on July 1, the Xinhua news agency said on Friday.

Radio and television station leaders should give priority to positive reports, improve programme quality and "stick to the correct orientation", the official agency quoted Ding Guangen, a member of the Communist Party's elite Politburo, as saying.

"Journalists should help create a favorable atmosphere for the resumption of the exercise of sovereignty over Hong Kong and the holding of the 15th Congress of the Communist Party of China," it quoted Ding as saying.

Analysts say Beijing is determined to ensure the return of Hong Kong to the motherland after 156 years of colonial British rule is seen by the Chinese people as a final end to national humiliation by foreign powers.
Social stability is also being stressed in the months leading up to the 15th party congress, a crucial gathering of the ruling party later this year.

Broadcasters should also make great efforts to push ideological progress and report advanced workers' meritorious deeds, Xinhua quoted Ding, who is also head of the Communist Party's propaganda department, as saying.
Radio and television stations should advocate the ideas of serving the people, patriotism, collectivism and socialism, while guiding the people to a correct outlook, he said.
